slot.brief: Solve a first-order linear DE dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) where P(x) is a rational function needing an integrating factor e^(integral); answer y = f(x) + C.

stem: For $x>0$, the general solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{2x+1}{x(x+1)}y=\dfrac{1}{x^2+1}$ is:

verdicts.working: The integrating factor is x(x+1). Thus [x(x+1)y]' = (x²+x)/(x²+1), whose integral is x + ½ln(x²+1) − tan⁻¹x + C. Dividing by x(x+1) gives option A.

working:
$\text{I.F.}=e^{\int(1/x+1/(x+1))\,dx}=x(x+1)$
$\dfrac{d}{dx}[x(x+1)y]=\dfrac{x(x+1)}{x^2+1}=1+\dfrac{x-1}{x^2+1}$
$x(x+1)y=x+\dfrac12\ln(x^2+1)-\tan^{-1}x+C$

Independent check: The integrating factor is x(x+1). Thus [x(x+1)y]' = (x²+x)/(x²+1), whose integral is x + ½ln(x²+1) − tan⁻¹x + C. Dividing by x(x+1) gives option A.
solution:
The integrating factor is $e^{\int(1/x+1/(x+1))\,dx}=x(x+1)$. Hence
$$[x(x+1)y]'=\frac{x(x+1)}{x^2+1}=1+\frac{x-1}{x^2+1}.$$
Integrating and dividing by $x(x+1)$ gives $y=\dfrac{x+\frac12\ln(x^2+1)-\tan^{-1}x+C}{x(x+1)}$, option (B).
